tools.name: connect
tools.description: Start using Avokata. With NO arguments it connects at once: no email, no signup, no key; call it first if the other tools are not visible. To keep work across chats, pass the user's email and language: one email with a Confirm link and a six-digit code, then call connect_verify(request_id).

tools.name: connect_verify
tools.description: Finish signing in: call right after connect(email) with the request_id and no code; it waits for the user's Confirm click (if it returns waiting, call again, never ask the user). Or pass the code they read you. Also takes a key the user already holds (api_key) to use that account here.

tools.name: avokata_account
tools.description: The signed-in account: status, the plans (record which one the user would choose; nothing is charged during the beta), keys and key revocation, and deletion.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Who the server thinks you are, which quotas you have left, and which jurisdictions currently have a corpus.

tools.name: describe

tools.description: Find the statutory provision (teisės akto straipsnis) that governs a question. PASS THE QUERY IN LITHUANIAN. The corpus is Lithuanian law in Lithuanian; an English query is not translated for you and does not work - measured 2026-08-28 on 23 questions a lawyer had answered from the corpus, Lithuania

tools.name: search_practice
tools.description: Find court practice (teismų praktika) on a legal question or a provision - rulings and judgments (nutartys ir sprendimai) as the courts published them. tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: List the playbooks available: the ones Avokata ships and any this account has written. Call this when you want the procedure for a legal task rather than inventing one.

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: Get one playbook in full: the procedure, the tools it expects you to call, and what the answer has to carry.

findings.detail: Description of "connect_verify" references sensitive artifacts (api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "connect_verify" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "search_law" is 1467 chars, far longer than this server's median (291). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: connect_verify, notifications · Private data: avokata_account · Public sink: connect, connect_verify, submit_feedback, notifications · Destructive: notifications.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: connect_verify, notifications · Private data: avokata_account · Public sink: connect, connect_verify, submit_feedback, notifications · Destructive: notifications

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
